clue.text: Healing doctor claimed with popular injection

indicators.note: the second piece is injected into the rearranged letters, which open up to take it
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of 'claimed' are rearranged

parts.note: IN means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A medic, said to be well liked, gives a therapeutic jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the medic of the surface but is the anagram signal; 'injection' says the popular piece goes into the rearranged letters (MEDIC-IN-AL).
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal is an adjective for remedies with curative power, as healing ones have.

clue.text: Some play that can generate heat?

definitions.meaning: a game or contest, as in tennis or football
a small stick tipped to strike a flame

explanation.definitionFit: A game between sides and a striking stick for lighting fire share one word.

clue.text: Blameworthy conduct done in holding me up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole result is read from bottom to top
the word for done in holds the word me inside it

parts.note: done in means exhausted, tired

explanation.surface: Someone worn out by holding a person up is accused of misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal makes DEMERIT from TIMERED; 'done in' reads as part of the surface's story of exhaustion but is the container word.
explanation.definitionFit: A black mark or fault against a person records behaviour deserving blame.

clue.text: Flier's quickest way to base?

parts.note: reads as a pilot heading home fast, but describes a submarine's emergency plunge to the depths, a submariner's own kind of diving

explanation.definitionFit: A rapid emergency submergence by a submarine is the fastest route to the sea bed.

clue.text: Beauty treatment at one's fingertips

parts.note: 'at one's fingertips' sounds like readily available, but literally it is the cosmetic painted onto the tips of the fingers

explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer for the fingernails is a cosmetic applied right at the ends of the fingers.

clue.text: Where many a salt is created

definitions.text: Where many a salt is created

parts.words: Where many a salt is created
parts.note: a salt suggests a sailor, but here it is a chemical compound made in a laboratory

explanation.definitionFit: Chemical salts are prepared by chemists in a laboratory, shortened to a three-letter word.

clue.text: Horse runs alongside river

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A horse gallops beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' suggests a racehorse, but it is a clothes horse, a frame for drying laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse and a drying rack for laundry are the same household frame.

clue.text: Bail possibly granted one to get a defence

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be ordered another way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A suspect granted bail hopes to build a defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of having been elsewhere when the crime happened is an accused person's excuse.

clue.text: Prepare for another job on Express, say

parts.note: RE means on, concerning
an express is a kind of fast train

explanation.surface: Someone prepares for a new career while commuting on the express.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a newspaper name, but it is an express train, given as an example by 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn new skills for different work is to be taught again.

clue.text: Criticise traveller's man in distress

parts.note: a commercial traveller is a sales rep

indicators.note: the word for man goes inside the word for distress

parts.note: to rend is to tear, as in heart-rending distress
HE stands for a man

explanation.surface: A salesman finds a man in trouble and scolds him.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke or censure someone is to criticise them.

clue.text: Instruments arranged in main pit

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a different order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Musical instruments are laid out in the main orchestra pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums are percussion instruments, played as a set in an orchestra.

clue.text: Pieced together description of New York?

definitions.meaning: an area dense with buildings, as Manhattan is

explanation.definitionFit: Something constructed has been raised in parts; a city crowded with buildings is described as densely developed.

clue.text: Right in the middle of a mess? Tough!

indicators.note: the letter for right sits within the word for a mess

parts.note: to make a hash of something is to make a mess of it

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a muddle is told bluntly to put up with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe, unkind manner or treatment is called tough or rough.

clue.text: Protect against disease caught at home half-way through leave

indicators.note: the inserted letters go into the middle of the word for leave, after its first three letters

parts.note: to vacate a place is to leave it
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
IN means at home

explanation.surface: Someone home on leave catches an illness midway and needs protecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Inoculating someone gives them immunity, guarding them against an infection.

clue.text: Help with moving furniture, darling? Fine, that's sweet

parts.note: a caster is a small wheel under furniture that makes it easier to move
sugar is an endearment, like darling

explanation.surface: Someone helping shift furniture is thanked as a darling: fine, that's sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: CASTER SUGAR is the fine-grained white sugar British cooks use for baking.
explanation.definitionFit: This very fine granulated product is a sweetener.

clue.text: Serve time that finishes sentence?

parts.note: to do time is to serve a prison sentence, so DO stands for serve

explanation.surface: A prisoner serving time asks what finally ends the sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' suggests a prison term after 'Serve time', but it is a written sentence ended by a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is a point of punctuation closing a written sentence.

clue.text: Capricious Liberal applied to be taken up by another party

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: something applied has been used
the Tories, the Conservatives, are another political party

explanation.surface: A fickle Liberal is drawn into a rival party.
explanation.walkthrough: L plus USED gives LUSED, which 'to be taken up' turns into DESUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Desultory means random and unmethodical, lacking a steady plan, much like changeable whims.

clue.text: Desire changes in nice new custom-built home

indicators.note: the rearranged letters of desire go inside the other rearranged group
something custom-built is made to a new design, so these letters are rebuilt in another order
changes here is a verb: the letters of desire change their order

explanation.surface: A buyer's wish shifts towards a pleasant, freshly built bespoke house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the desire letters into RESIDE; 'custom-built' rebuilds the other group as INNCE, which wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being officially living at a place, as a writer installed at a college is, means being at home there.

clue.text: Wexford could be spot I have seen

parts.note: to spot something is to detect it
contracted to I've, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone thinks Wexford might be a place they once noticed and visited.
explanation.walkthrough: Wexford looks like the Irish county, but it is Inspector Wexford, Ruth Rendell's fictional policeman; 'could be' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Wexford is a fictional police investigator, an example of the type.

clue.text: Same old race I'd entered? Answer's obvious

parts.note: self once meant same, an old sense of the word

indicators.note: the letters for I'd go into the word for a race

parts.note: a race is a sporting event
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone watching the same old race asks if they entered; the reply is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Same old' reads as a weary phrase, but 'old' marks an obsolete sense: self meaning same.
explanation.definitionFit: A truth needing no proof is plain and apparent.

clue.text: Crackpot's poor at cluing, being without gravity

indicators.note: poor means badly done, so the letters are rearranged
the letter for gravity is removed from the fodder

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravity's acceleration

explanation.surface: A crossword critic says someone is mad: their clueing is poor and lacks seriousness.
explanation.definitionFit: A madman or eccentric is called a crackpot.

clue.text: Wander around tribal territory

definitions.meaning: the land of one of the twelve tribes of Israel, named after Jacob's son

explanation.definitionFit: Roaming idly is to gallivant; in the Bible one of Israel's twelve tribes and its land share a son of Jacob's name.

clue.text: English rules, say, force butter substitute endlessly up.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the combined pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ram is to force

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: marge is British slang for margarine

explanation.surface: A rule of English is to push a butter alternative upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: RAM plus MARG gives RAMMARG, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The rules of a language such as English make up its structure; 'say' marks English as one example.

clue.text: Pirate's underwear

definitions.meaning: belonging to Long John Silver, the pirate of Treasure Island

explanation.definitionFit: Long-legged warm underpants share their name with Stevenson's one-legged buccaneer in the possessive.

clue.text: Jack takes one of the family for an outing

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
an aunt is a family member

explanation.surface: Jack brings along a relative for a day out.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pleasure trip is an excursion or outing.

clue.text: Resounding noise of Conservative tedious to Scots?

parts.note: lang is the Scots form of long, which can mean tedious

explanation.surface: A Tory drones on so long that Scottish listeners hear only noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing metallic sound is a resounding noise.

clue.text: Lass, not half thin, lacks length in this

definitions.text: Lass, not half thin, lacks length in this

indicators.note: the word for lass loses the letter for length

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: only half of the word thin is kept, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A girl who is far from slim falls short on this measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: GIR (lass without L) plus TH (half of 'thin'); the whole clue also describes a plump girl short of inches.
explanation.definitionFit: The measurement round the waist is what a stout girl has plenty of.

clue.text: Advance forcefully or debut could be wasted

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer either pushes forward hard or their first night could be thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' is a link: the anagram signal is 'wasted'.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrust oneself forward unwelcomely is to push oneself forcefully on others.

clue.text: Non-Liberal peer gets attention

indicators.note: non- attached to Liberal means without it, so the L is removed

parts.note: an earl is a peer

explanation.surface: A peer who is not a Liberal receives notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is to give heed, listening attention.

clue.text: Good miler's out, taking in miles in dim light

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for miles
out means wrong or not in place, so the letters of the runner are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A fine middle-distance runner, out running in the dusk, covers the miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MILER into LIMER, and 'taking in' puts M within it: LIM-M-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint, wavering gleam is a weak or dim light.

clue.text: Most of the island backed this vessel

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the whole combined run is read backwards
all but the last letter of the word 'the' is kept

parts.note: a cay is a small low island

explanation.surface: Most of the islanders backed this boat.
explanation.walkthrough: TH (most of 'the') plus CAY gives THCAY, which 'backed' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat used for pleasure or racing is a vessel.

clue.text: Unusual change of heart producing chemical discovery

parts.note: rare means unusual

indicators.note: a change of the word's letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rare change of heart leads to a breakthrough in the chemistry lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' looks like a set phrase, but 'change of' is the anagram signal on HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanthanide oxides were found as new elements by chemists, so such a group is a chemical discovery.
